claims.text: Role in CRPS: topical lidocaine (or capsaicin) may be used for neuropathic pain in early CRPS w mild to moderate Sx;
claims.quote: Topical lidocaine or capsaicin creams may be used for treating neuropathic pain in early CRPS with mild to moderate symptoms

claims.text: evidence is limited, and local burning or irritation may limit use.
claims.quote: though evidence of their efficacy is limited, and local side effects like burning and irritation may restrict their use

claims.text: Lidocaine patch (Lidoderm) dose: Apply to intact skin over the most painful area; max 3 patches once for up to 12 h within a 24-h period.
claims.quote: Apply LIDODERM to intact skin to cover the most painful area. Apply the prescribed number of patches (maximum of 3), only once for up to 12 hours within a 24 hour period.

claims.text: If irritation/burning occurs during application, remove patch(es) and do not reapply until irritation subsides.
claims.quote: If irritation or a burning sensation occurs during application, remove the patch(es) and do not reapply until the irritation subsides.

claims.text: Avoid water contact (bathing, swimming, showering) — LIDODERM may not stick if it gets wet.
claims.quote: LIDODERM may not stick if it gets wet. Avoid contact with water, such as bathing, swimming or showering.

claims.text: Lidocaine patch (Lidoderm) application/handling safety: Keep out of reach of children/pets; fold used patches so adhesive sticks to itself and discard safely.
claims.quote: Fold used patches so that the adhesive side sticks to itself and safely discard used patches or pieces of cut patches where children and pets cannot get to them. LIDODERM should be kept out of the reach of children.

claims.text: CI: known Hx of sensitivity to amide-type local anesthetics or other components.
claims.quote: LIDODERM is contraindicated in patients with a known history of sensitivity to local anesthetics of the amide type, or to any other component of the product.

claims.text: Lidocaine patch (Lidoderm) warnings: Methemoglobinemia: susceptible pts incl G6PD deficiency, congenital/idiopathic methemoglobinemia, cardiac/pulmonary compromise, infants <6 months, concurrent oxidizing agents.
claims.quote: Although all patients are at risk for methemoglobinemia, patients with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency, congenital or idiopathic methemoglobinemia, cardiac or pulmonary compromise, infants under 6 months of age, and concurrent exposure to oxidizing agents or their metabolites are more susceptible to developing clinical manifestations of the condition.

claims.text: Immediate tx required to avert CNS/CV effects (seizures, coma, arrhythmias, death); discontinue LIDODERM and any other oxidizing agents.
claims.quote: Methemoglobin levels may continue to rise; therefore, immediate treatment is required to avert more serious central nervous system and cardiovascular adverse effects, including seizures, coma, arrhythmias, and death. Discontinue LIDODERM and any other oxidizing agents.

claims.text: Even a used patch contains ≥665 mg lidocaine — small child or pet may suffer serious effects from chewing or ingesting a new or used patch.
claims.quote: used LIDODERM patch contains a large amount of lidocaine (at least 665 mg). The potential exists for a small child or a pet to suffer serious adverse effects from chewing or ingesting a new or used LIDODERM patch

claims.text: Excessive dosing (larger areas or longer than recommended wearing time) may ↑ absorption and blood concentrations → serious adverse effects.
claims.quote: Excessive dosing by applying LIDODERM to larger areas or for longer than the recommended wearing time could result in increased absorption of lidocaine and high blood concentrations, leading to serious adverse effects

claims.text: Lidocaine toxicity expected at blood concentrations above 5 mcg/mL.
claims.quote: Lidocaine toxicity could be expected at lidocaine blood concentrations above 5 mcg/mL.

claims.text: Lidocaine patch (Lidoderm) precautions, interactions, overdose: Severe hepatic disease ↑ risk of toxic blood concentrations (impaired metabolism).
claims.quote: Patients with severe hepatic disease are at greater risk of developing toxic blood concentrations of lidocaine, because of their inability to metabolize lidocaine normally.

claims.text: Apply only to intact skin; application to broken/inflamed skin may ↑ blood concentrations.
claims.quote: Application to broken or inflamed skin, although not tested, may result in higher blood concentrations of lidocaine from increased absorption. LIDODERM is only recommended for use on intact skin.

claims.text: Use caution w Class I antiarrhythmics (tocainide, mexiletine) — toxic effects additive and potentially synergistic.
claims.quote: LIDODERM should be used with caution in patients receiving Class I antiarrhythmic drugs (such as tocainide and mexiletine) since the toxic effects are additive and potentially synergistic.

claims.text: OD mgmt: close monitoring, supportive care, symptomatic treatment; dialysis of negligible value.
claims.quote: The management of overdose includes close monitoring, supportive care, and symptomatic treatment. Dialysis is of negligible value in the treatment of acute overdose with lidocaine.
